content.title: About
content.content: Cooked garlic consists of peeled garlic cloves that have been boiled until tender. Heat softens the sharp aroma, giving the cloves a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a creamy texture. It is commonly used as a side dish, in sauces, soups, and purees.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cooked garlic is easier on the digestive system than raw garlic.
Thermal processing reduces allicin, the compound responsible for the pungent smell.
In many cuisines, cooked garlic is blended into a paste with olive oil and herbs.
Garlic belongs to the Liliaceae family and is a close relative of onion, leek, and shallot.
Cooked garlic can be kept in the refrigerator for up to a week and frozen for several months.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Garlic contains sulfur compounds such as diallyl disulfide that may enhance the body’s immune defenses.

items.title: Blood pressure reduction
items.content: Studies suggest regular garlic consumption can contribute to modest reductions in blood pressure.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Cooked garlic retains vitamin C and selenium, which help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Cardiovascular health
items.content: Garlic sulfides may improve lipid profiles by lowering LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: The soft texture of cooked garlic is easy to digest and may promote beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to garlic, ranging from skin rashes to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Garlic can enhance the effects of anticoagulant drugs, so caution is advised for people on blood‑thinners.

items.title: Heartburn and discomfort
items.content: Sensitive people may experience heartburn or gas after large portions of cooked garlic.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked garlic can be served as a simple snack, added to purees, sauces, salads, casseroles, and soups. It also works well mashed into a paste with olive oil, lemon, and herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked garlic in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 3 months. Check for off‑odors or texture changes before use and discard any spoiled pieces.
